clue.text: Again sat and rested

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again
to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat gives posed

explanation.surface: Someone sat down once more and had a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To repose is to lie or sit at ease, so having reposed is having taken a rest.

clue.text: Precipitate artist finishes in the lake

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist
a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: A painter ends up falling into the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes' is a link: the artist finishes up in the lake. 'Precipitate' is a noun here, what falls from clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: Water falling from the sky is precipitation, the meteorological term for what falls from clouds.

clue.text: Women commonly expect to become members of this club

definitions.text: Women commonly expect to become members of this club

parts.words: Women commonly expect to become members of this club
parts.note: commonly flags slang: a woman who is expecting a baby is said in British slang to be in this club

explanation.surface: A remark about women joining a society.
explanation.walkthrough: To be in the pudding club is British slang for being pregnant; 'expect' hints at expecting a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase for pregnancy names a club after a dessert, which women who are expecting are said to join.

clue.text: Ex's ground for divorce?

parts.note: a partner switching gender may be grounds to divorce; also the letters of Ex's ground up give a three-letter word meaning gender

explanation.surface: A former spouse's reason for ending the marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffling EXS gives SEX, so 'ground' is a hint at a change to the letters as well as the legal ground for divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: A gender-reassignment operation could be the reason a spouse seeks to end a marriage.

clue.text: Double fare for old bird

indicators.note: double means the word is written twice in a row

parts.note: to fare is to do, as in 'how did you do?'

explanation.surface: Twice the usual meal for an ancient fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a flightless bird of Mauritius, extinct since the 1600s.

clue.text: Sort of dividend to remit in loose change

indicators.note: change here is the anagram signal, and loose suggests letters set free to fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to send a payment in coins rather than notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose change' reads as coins, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of REMIT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim dividend is one paid partway through a company's financial year, before the final one.

clue.text: Supervise candidates in exam — one may be leaving it

definitions.text: Supervise candidates in exam — one may be leaving it

parts.words: Supervise candidates in exam — one may be leaving it
parts.note: the official who watches over examinees must also keep an eye on any candidate who walks out of the hall

explanation.surface: Overseeing students sitting a test while someone tries to walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigilate is to keep watch over people sitting a written test.

clue.text: Works cash registers

explanation.surface: A shop's checkout machines described as operating.
explanation.definitionFit: To till land is to work it with a plough, and tills are the drawers or machines that hold a shop's takings.

clue.text: Not against really Parisian clothes

indicators.note: not means the letter for against is left out of the French word

parts.note: vraiment is French for really
V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A remark that Parisian fashion is honestly not opposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments or attire.

clue.text: Doctor has to cock an ear to VIP

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

indicators.note: to cock is to turn upwards, so in a down clue the ear word is read bottom to top

parts.note: lug is slang for an ear

explanation.surface: A physician has to listen hard to an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful, important figure, like a business magnate.

clue.text: First digit shows the positions of entries

explanation.surface: A finger pointing out where things are listed.
explanation.definitionFit: The index finger is the first digit after the thumb, and a book's index lists where its entries appear.

clue.text: Doing menial work for others when it's broiling

explanation.surface: Someone stuck with drudgery for others on a sweltering day.
explanation.walkthrough: In British law a junior barrister devils for a senior one; in cookery to devil is to grill food with hot spices.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilling is drudge work done for an employer, and devilled food is grilled with a peppery seasoning, so broiling with spice is devilling.

clue.text: Wriggle out of court order by the Governor

parts.note: a writ is a written order issued by a court
HE, His Excellency, is the formal style of a colonial governor

explanation.surface: A colonial official trying to escape a legal summons.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, the same motion as a wriggle.

clue.text: Where the early bird is likely 'to be found

definitions.text: Where the early bird is likely 'to be found

parts.words: Where the early bird is likely 'to be found
parts.note: the early bird of the proverb is up at dawn, but read literally a bird at its earliest stage is still unhatched inside its casing

explanation.surface: Asking where to find the bird that catches the worm.
explanation.definitionFit: A chick before hatching is enclosed in the hard casing of its egg.

clue.text: Shakespearian schoolmaster makes us see plant among weeds,

indicators.note: among means the middle pieces sit within the outer word

parts.note: to weed a bed is to hoe it, so weeds as a verb gives hoes
lo is an old exclamation bidding us look
a fern is a plant

explanation.surface: A teacher from a Shakespeare play gets pupils to spot a plant in a weedy patch.
explanation.walkthrough: Holofernes is the pedant schoolmaster in Love's Labour's Lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Holofernes is the pompous teacher character in Love's Labour's Lost.

clue.text: Hybrid animal can about turn

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a can is a tin
your turn in a game is your go

explanation.surface: A crossbred beast able to wheel round on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the offspring of a male tiger and a lioness, a crossbreed of two big cats.

clue.text: Bound to be confined to school with awful boil

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of boil are in a terrible mess and must be rearranged

parts.note: a pupil who is gated is kept within school grounds as a punishment

explanation.surface: A pupil kept in after school while suffering from a nasty boil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' turns BOIL into OBLI. Gated is British school slang for being confined to the premises as punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Being obligated is being duty-bound to do something.

clue.text: Her husband keeps going on courses

definitions.text: Her husband keeps going on courses

parts.words: Her husband keeps going on courses
parts.note: courses seem educational, but they are where a sport with clubs and eighteen holes is played, leaving the wife alone

explanation.surface: A wife whose spouse is always away on training courses.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose husband spends all his time playing on the links is jokingly said to be bereaved by the game.

clue.text: The 'ornamental sword came with the Danes originally

indicators.note: originally hints that the letters of the two words are to be restored to some other order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A decorative blade said to have arrived with the Viking invaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' tells you to rearrange CAME and DANES together.
explanation.definitionFit: A Damascus blade is a sword of patterned, decorated steel, named after the city of Damascus.

clue.text: Knock opponent's ball outside .. because it's on the board

indicators.note: outside means the first piece is wrapped round the second

parts.note: in croquet to roquet is to strike another player's ball with your own
for can mean because, as in 'for he was tired'

explanation.surface: A croquet shot sending a rival's ball out of play, recorded on the scoreboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a cheeseboard, not a scoreboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Roquefort is a French blue cheese, served on a cheeseboard.

clue.text: Searched for Adela in the Caves of Marabar

definitions.text: Adela in the Caves of Marabar

explanation.surface: A literary search inside the caves from A Passage to India.
explanation.walkthrough: Adela Quested is the young Englishwoman in E. M. Forster's A Passage to India whose visit to the Marabar Caves drives the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To quest is to go seeking something, and Forster's heroine Adela bears that surname.

clue.text: Sailor loses his head acting as a doctor

indicators.note: loses his head means the first letter of the sailor's name is dropped

parts.note: Joshua Slocum was the first person to sail alone round the world

explanation.surface: A seaman decapitated while pretending to be a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailor is the famous lone circumnavigator Joshua Slocum.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a stand-in who temporarily acts in place of a regular GP or medical practitioner.

clue.text: Sudden change of mind about the cost

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
the cost of something is its price

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly reconsidering when told what it will cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a whim, an impulsive switch of mood or plan.

clue.text: It would surprise Dr Johnson if — this were a woman on her hind legs

definitions.text: It would surprise Dr Johnson if — this were a woman on her hind legs

parts.words: It would surprise Dr Johnson if — this were a woman on her hind legs
parts.note: Samuel Johnson said a female sermon-giver was like a dog walking on its hind legs: not done well, but surprising to see done at all

explanation.surface: A nod to Samuel Johnson's famous quip about women standing up to deliver sermons.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson's remark was about a woman delivering sermons from the pulpit, which is the minister's role.

clue.text: Walker run over when facing the other way

indicators.note: facing the other way means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to run over something is to recap it

explanation.surface: A pedestrian knocked down by a car reversing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run over' looks like a road accident but means summarise.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is one who walks steadily or sets the pace on foot.

clue.text: Name carrying little weight in church do

indicators.note: in means the weight sits inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
oz, an ounce, is a small weight

explanation.surface: Someone of little importance at a church function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a party at the church, but it is a verb meaning cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To cozen is to trick or swindle, as in 'do someone out of their money'.

clue.text: Steals some beer

explanation.surface: A thief pinching some ale.
explanation.definitionFit: To swipe is slang for to pinch or steal, and swipes is an old word for thin, weak beer.

clue.text: He heralds the end for Old Jolyon!

indicators.note: the end for the name means the run is taken from its final letters

explanation.surface: Proclaiming the death of Old Jolyon from the Forsyte Saga.
explanation.walkthrough: Lyon King of Arms is the chief herald of Scotland; Old Jolyon is a character in Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Lyon is Scotland's chief officer of arms, who makes proclamations as a herald.

clue.text: Urban dwellers or countrymen?

explanation.surface: Asking whether town folk or rural folk are meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'countrymen' tempts you towards rural people, but it means fellow nationals.
explanation.definitionFit: The citizens of a city are town dwellers, and the citizens of a nation are compatriots.

clue.text: Spur road

explanation.surface: A short side road branching off a main one.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on is to urge or push them, and a private road up to a house is called a drive.

clue.text: Rats, not Reds, defect

indicators.note: defect suggests the letters desert their places and regroup

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Informers who are not communists switching sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats' and 'defect' suggest traitors changing sides; 'defect' tells you to rearrange NOT REDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats are gnawing mammals of the order Rodentia.

clue.text: The source of Morris's news

parts.note: William Morris wrote a utopian novel titled News from a place that does not exist

explanation.surface: Asking where a man named Morris got his information.
explanation.walkthrough: William Morris, the Victorian designer and socialist, wrote the utopian novel News from Nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Morris's novel takes its title from an imaginary land, a place that exists in no location.
